summary: Master humanitarian digital communication. Learn CWC strategies, OCHA data responsibility, and crisis engagement tools. Enroll for expert-led training.
lede: Digital Communication in Humanitarian Aid helps organizations build reliable two-way communication with people affected by crises. The course covers digital information needs assessments, secure feedback systems, misinformation management, cross-platform data privacy, and engagement reporting to support transparent and accountable operations. You will work with tools such as KoboToolbox and RapidPro, configure messaging APIs for crisis response, and explore AI-driven sentiment analysis for monitoring community needs. The training also addresses low-bandwidth settings, security risks, the digital divide, and the balance between urgent response, data governance, and digital inclusion.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level course is essential for professionals who manage information flows and community relationships in humanitarian contexts.
modules: Digital Humanitarianism and the Core Humanitarian Standard
Messaging Apps and Chatbots in Crisis
Digital Ethics and the Signal Code
prerequisites: Participants should have at least two years of experience in humanitarian response, communications, or information management. Familiarity with basic data collection tools and a working knowledge of the humanitarian cluster system is recommended.
